vocab.definition: no atoms are made or lost in a reaction.
same number of each atom on both sides.
a substance that reacts (left of the arrow).
a substance made (right of the arrow).

misconceptions.wrong: Mass is lost when a gas is given off.
misconceptions.right: The gas escapes — but its mass is not destroyed.

misconceptions.wrong: You can change subscripts to balance.

misconceptions.right: Mass seems to fall — gases escape into the air.

infoPanels.title: WORKED EXAMPLE
workedSteps: 12 g of carbon reacts with 32 g of oxygen.
No atoms are lost — mass is conserved.

questions.text: State the law of conservation of mass. [1 mark]
8 g of methane reacts with 32 g of oxygen to make 22 g of CO₂. Calculate the mass of water made. [2 marks]
Explain why the mass appears to decrease when a metal carbonate is heated. [2 marks]
Explain why magnesium gains mass when burned in air. [2 marks]
Explain why mass stays constant when a reaction is done in a sealed flask. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Atoms are only rearranged — total mass before = total mass after.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does burning in an open dish seem to break the law of conservation of mass?
